verdict.rationale: Jules can turn a GitHub issue into a task when the issue gets the "jules" label. It then generates a plan that can be reviewed before any code changes, which loosely amounts to a structured task with proposed scope. However, the plan is a code-implementation plan for a single task, and nothing shows Jules ingesting raw user-feedback submissions or producing structured task breakdowns or scope definitions for product managers. Missing for 10: ingestion of user feedback submissions beyond labeled GitHub issues, structured task decomposition from feedback, explicit scope proposals aimed at PM workflows, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a product-manager, I can convert user feedback submissions into structured tasks with proposed scope

citations.quote: Use the "jules" label in an issue to assign a task directly in GitHub.
Once you submit a task, Jules will generate a plan. You can review and approve it before any code changes are made.
